clue.text: Unusual celibacy without a mode of transport

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged
'without' means lacking, so the following word's letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A monk's unusual vow of chastity apparently leaves him stranded with no way to get about.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle is a pedal vehicle, one of the commonest ways of getting around.

clue.text: Infant left in tower

blocks.note: a babe is a baby
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A baby has been abandoned in some tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of Babel is the biblical tower whose builders were struck with confused languages.

clue.text: Deer looking out of car I bought

indicators.note: something looking out of a place peeps from inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the first three words and the start of the fourth

explanation.surface: A deer gazes out of the window of a car someone has just purchased.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large member of the deer family.

clue.text: Bivouac where East Anglian river’s quiet

blocks.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge in East Anglia
p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Campers choose a tranquil spot on a riverbank in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England around Norfolk, Suffolk and Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivouac is a temporary encampment, so a synonym for a camp.

clue.text: Kind of activity involving adultery between academics?

definitions.text: Kind of activity involving adultery between academics?

blocks.note: surface reading: a scandalous affair in a university common room
setter's reading: affairs are 'extra' to marriage, and among academics they lie outside the course of study, like clubs and sports

explanation.surface: Gossip about lecturers having affairs with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke blends extramarital with the school term for anything done outside timetabled lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes pursuits outside the regular course of study, such as societies and sport.

clue.text: Revise a text such as: "Get the bus back before the tide turns"

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
when something turns its letters are churned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor tidies a sentence about catching a bus home before the tide comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted sentence looks like the text being revised, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for publication, as a newspaper subeditor does.

clue.text: Upright, slim, on the way to a better life

definitions.text: on the way to a better life

blocks.note: first meaning: morally correct, the path of honest living
both halves of the phrase mean narrow, an extra hint linking the meanings

blocks.clueFragment: on the way to a better life
blocks.note: second meaning: the strait gate and narrow way that lead to heaven in Matthew's gospel

explanation.surface: A description of a lean, virtuous pilgrim heading for salvation.
explanation.walkthrough: Strait is an old word for narrow, from the biblical 'strait is the gate, and narrow is the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the path of moral rectitude, the virtuous route said to lead to heaven.

clue.text: Means of having a choice in the poll?

blocks.note: by means 'by means of', as in travelling by train
an election is the act of choosing

explanation.surface: A question about how voters get to choose when they go to the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of voting, but 'poll' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a by-election is a vote held to fill one parliamentary seat that falls vacant between general elections.

clue.text: Radical art disc playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and moved about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An experimental record of avant-garde music is being played.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe measures that are extreme and far-reaching in effect.

clue.text: Lever on which the French step first

indicators.note: first tells us the second item named is placed ahead of the other

blocks.note: to tread is to step
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A description of a foot-operated mechanism that French people press before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on which' reads naturally after Lever, since you press a treadle with your foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-worked lever driving a machine such as an old sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Confused Robert and me with a measuring instrument

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a gadget has baffled both them and their friend Robert.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer is an instrument gauging atmospheric pressure, used to forecast weather.

clue.text: Delete Times at one point

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
E (east) is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the Times at some moment, like an editor cutting a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Times look like the newspaper; it is just periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to rub it out or wipe it away, as with deleting.

clue.text: Look at live part of organ

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine a living piece of some bodily organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded section of an organ, such as the lungs, liver or brain.

clue.text: Custom's document Edward revealed

blocks.note: a manifest is the cargo list shown to customs officers
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward's paperwork at customs exposed what he was carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifested means made plain or shown openly, so it matches revealed as a past tense.

clue.text: Plant a piece of land

blocks.note: a herb is a kind of plant
a garden is a plot of land

explanation.surface: An instruction to sow a plot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a patch of ground you plant up.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb garden is a plot set aside for growing culinary and medicinal herbs.

clue.text: Old city boyfriend covered for the department

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a beau is a boyfriend
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A boyfriend stood in for someone working in an old city's department.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a government office or agency, such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

clue.text: Item in broadcast recital

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece included in a concert that went out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a single thing or object, as in an article of clothing.

clue.text: Chapter on supple mountaineer

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
limber means flexible

explanation.surface: A book chapter about an agile alpinist.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber is someone who scales mountains or rock faces, so a mountaineer.

clue.text: He’s into cores and bonds

indicators.note: going into something places one item inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some man is keen on apple cores and stocks and shares.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together, the verb sense of bonding.

clue.text: Poultice cub eats partly in cooler

indicators.note: partly says only a portion of the run of words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A young animal is caught eating its medical dressing inside a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cubes are dropped into drinks to chill them, so they act as coolers.

clue.text: Sagging with exhaustion because of poor return in a lost day

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
lost means gone missing, so the letter before it disappears from the next word
in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is wilting after a disappointing comeback during a wasted day.
explanation.walkthrough: D(ROOP)Y: the reversed word sits in the day that has lost its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy means hanging down limply, which is how a tired person or wilted flower looks.

clue.text: Job for old pupil returning as pacifier

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a place is a position or job
OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy comes back to take up a post as a peacemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment given to soothe a patient rather than cure, hence something that pacifies.

clue.text: Relating to rank of unfortunate archer in hailstorm

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone awry, so the letters are set out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
the frozen precipitation, whose storm also tosses its letters about with the rest

explanation.surface: A luckless bowman gets caught out in a downpour of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Hailstorm looks like one word, but it splits into fodder and a second signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Hierarchal describes a system ordered in ranks or grades, an alternative form of hierarchical.

clue.text: Information describing a third activist, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the leading letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Some details describing the third member of a group of campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a charade with 'third' picking a letter, but just the word heads are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for analysis, so information.

clue.text: Judge almost all animals

indicators.note: almost all of something is everything but its tail end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to assess is to judge

explanation.surface: A judge almost all the animals at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all animals' reads as one phrase, but the split falls before animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are donkeys, hoofed animals related to horses.

clue.text: Otherwise live in mask?

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether one might live another life behind a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a covering that conceals the face, as a mask does.

clue.text: Drinks for everyone or a single shot?

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of drinks bought for the whole group at the bar
second meaning: one bullet or cartridge for a gun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Single shot' tempts toward a measure of spirits in a pub; it is ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a buying of drinks for everyone present and one piece of ammunition.

clue.text: Great headland's great size

blocks.note: large means great in size
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A description of how huge a big promontory is.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness is the quality of being big, a noun for bulk or extent.

clue.text: More severe back on East River

blocks.note: the stern is the back of a ship
E is the abbreviation for East
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Things grew harsher back on the East River in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: East River looks like the New York waterway, but it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, meaning stricter or harsher.

clue.text: William's shelter for old white trees

indicators.note: a shelter surrounds and protects what it holds, so one item goes inside another

blocks.note: Will is short for William, with the possessive s
O is the abbreviation for old
W is the abbreviation for white

explanation.surface: William provides cover for some aged white trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Willows are trees and shrubs of the genus Salix, often found by water.
